This approach leverages the strengths of each model type in handling structured vs. unstructured data. The separation allows for comparative analysis of how different data types influence prediction accuracy. The framework assumes that combining these models will yield superior results than any single model alone, supported by prior studies showing neural networks' effectiveness in sports prediction. The accuracy threshold of 70% surpasses the baseline of 60% established by Ottawa, indicating improved generalizability. However, this method may fail if the data lacks sufficient variance or if the models are overfitted to historical patterns. The dual nature of the problem—predicting binary outcomes while incorporating complex statistical features—requires careful calibration of model parameters and robust cross-validation strategies to prevent spurious correlations.
